quizzes.title: Investment, Support and Charging: MCQ
quizzes.passage: The Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi has notified the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy 2.0. The policy is scheduled to come into force from 1 July 2026 and to remain effective until 31 March 2030. It builds upon the achievements of the Delhi EV Policy 2020 and provides a comprehensive roadmap for transforming Delhi into a leading electric mobility hub. A central focus is reducing vehicular emissions by encouraging the electrification of high-usage and high-emission transport segments. The policy names several priority vehicle segments, including two-wheelers, three-wheelers, school buses, app-based aggregator fleets and government-owned transport fleets. The booklet presents the policy's major provisions under a dedicated heading, and these include timelines for vehicle registration. The booklet also outlines the expected benefits of electric vehicles. These include a likely fall in demand for petrol and diesel, the creation of new jobs in the automobile sector, and a reduction in pollution-induced health problems. The policy's provisions cover financial support and investment as well as infrastructure development, and each area is assigned to a separate implementing body.

questions.q: Government financial support under Delhi EV Policy 2.0 is restricted to which category of vehicles?
options: Battery electric vehicles only, not hybrid vehicles
Both battery electric and hybrid vehicles
questions.explanation: The booklet states that government support is restricted exclusively to battery electric vehicles and not to hybrid vehicles.

questions.q: How many public charging stations are planned to be installed across Delhi under the policy?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the policy plans installation of over 30,000 public charging stations across Delhi.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a key objective of Delhi EV Policy 2.0?
options: Phasing out all public transport within 5 years
Restricting private vehicle ownership in Delhi
questions.explanation: Strengthening charging and battery-swapping infrastructure is one of the key objectives listed in the booklet.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Hybrid vehicles are eligible for government financial support under Delhi EV Policy 2.0.
Reason (R): Government support under the policy is restricted exclusively to battery electric vehicles.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Support is restricted to battery electric vehicles, so the assertion is false while the reason is true.

questions.q: Which key objective of Delhi EV Policy 2.0 concerns public and commercial transport?
options: Encouraging sustainable public and commercial transport
Restricting private vehicle ownership in Delhi
Phasing out all public transport within 5 years
questions.explanation: The booklet lists encouraging sustainable public and commercial transport as a key objective.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Delhi EV Policy 2.0:
I. The policy plans installation of over 30,000 public charging stations across Delhi.
II. Reducing urban air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions is listed as a key objective.
III. Hybrid vehicles are eligible for government financial support.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while statement III contradicts the rule that support is limited to battery electric vehicles.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the key objectives of Delhi EV Policy 2.0:
Promoting widespread adoption of zero-emission vehicles.
Promoting hydrogen fuel cell vehicles.
Supporting India's clean energy and climate commitments.
Reducing urban air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Three statements are listed objectives, while promoting hydrogen fuel cell vehicles is not listed among them.

quizzes.title: National Schemes: NEMMP, FAME and PM E-DRIVE: MCQ
quizzes.passage: The booklet describes a set of national schemes that support electric vehicles, alongside its coverage of Delhi's own electric vehicle policy. Among these schemes is a broader national mission plan. FAME India is one of the schemes. Its purpose is to give a boost to the development of electric vehicles, and it works through three approaches: establishing charging stations, incentivising buyers and publicising the benefits of electric vehicles. The booklet lists the expected benefits of this push as a fall in the demand for petrol and diesel, the creation of new jobs in the automobile sector, and a reduction in pollution-induced health problems. PM E-DRIVE is the most recent of the schemes described. Its support covers electric buses, e-trucks, e-ambulances and other new emerging EV categories, and it is described as building on earlier efforts. Its objectives and nodal ministry are listed in a separate section of the booklet. Separately, the booklet notes that Delhi EV Policy 2.0 builds upon the achievements of Delhi EV Policy 2020 and is set to remain effective until 31 March 2030. The policy also describes electrification of high-usage and high-emission transport segments as a way to reduce vehicular emissions.

questions.q: In which year was the National Electric Mobility Mission Plan launched?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the National Electric Mobility Mission Plan was launched in 2013.

questions.q: Which ministry launched FAME India?
options: Ministry of Heavy Industries & Public Enterprises
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
questions.explanation: The booklet says FAME was launched by the Ministry of Heavy Industries & Public Enterprises.

questions.q: For which period is the PM E-DRIVE scheme set to run?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the PM E-DRIVE scheme period as 2024-2026.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): FAME India is a part of the National Electric Mobility Mission Plan.
Reason (R): Subsidies under FAME can be claimed for electric buses.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true in the booklet, but the subsidy eligibility does not explain why FAME is part of the mission plan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about national electric mobility schemes:
I. PM E-DRIVE builds on FAME-II and the Electric Mobility Promotion Scheme 2024.
II. FAME stands for Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles.
III. PM E-DRIVE was launched in 2013 along with the National Electric Mobility Mission Plan.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while statement III gives the wrong launch year for PM E-DRIVE, which was launched in 2024.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about FAME subsidies:
Subsidies can be claimed for two-wheelers.
Subsidies can be claimed only for two-wheelers.
Subsidies can be claimed for electric buses.
Subsidies can be claimed for hybrid cars.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists two-wheelers, electric buses and hybrid cars, so the statement that subsidies are only for two-wheelers is incorrect.

questions.q: Which of the following is eligible for support under PM E-DRIVE?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists electric two-wheelers among the vehicle categories eligible for PM E-DRIVE support.
